Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings ('target board' appearance)
Yellowing (chlorosis) surrounding the dark spots on older lower leaves
Premature leaf drop and reduced tuber yields
Potato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24°C - 29°C / 75°F - 85°F) with high humidity or alternating wet and dry weather.
organic_treatments: Copper Fungicides: Apply organic liquid copper soap every 7-10 days upon first sign.
Neem Oil: Spray cold-pressed neem oil (0.5% - 1.0% dilution) as a preventive bio-fungicide.
Bio-control Agent: Apply Bacillus subtilis (e.g., Serenade) to inhibit spore germination.
Pruning & Removal: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves to reduce inoculum spread.
chemical_treatments: Mancozeb 75% WP: Apply 2g per liter of water at 7-10 day intervals.
Chlorothalonil: 1.5 - 2.0 mL per liter as a protectant spray.
Azoxystrobin: Systemic fungicide applied for established early blight control.
prevention_tips: Crop Rotation: Rotate potatoes with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., corn, beans) on a 3-4 year cycle.
Drip Irrigation: Avoid overhead irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Plant Spacing: Ensure adequate spacing between plants to maximize airflow.
Resistant Varieties: Plant early-blight resistant cultivars.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked oily spots on leaf tips and margins
White cottony fungal growth on the underside of leaves during humid weather
Rapid wilting, browning, and collapse of entire vine within days
Tuber infection causing firm, reddish-brown dry rot under the skin
Potato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures (10°C - 20°C / 50°F - 68°F) with high relative humidity (>90%) and rain/fog.
organic_treatments: Bordeaux Mixture: Apply 1% Bordeaux mixture (Copper Sulfate + Hydrated Lime) preventively.
Copper Hydroxide: Spray fixed copper formulations weekly during high humidity weather.
Immediate Vine Destruction: Cut and destroy infected foliage 2 weeks before harvest to protect tubers.
chemical_treatments: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (e.g., Curzate): Curative and protective spray applied immediately after symptoms appear.
Metalaxyl / Mefenoxam + Mancozeb (e.g., Ridomil Gold): Systemic action against systemic late blight infection.
Dimethomorph or Fluazinam: Protectant sprays for high disease pressure periods.
prevention_tips: Certified Seed Tubers: Always plant disease-free certified seed potatoes.
Eliminate Volunteer Plants: Remove volunteer potato plants and cull piles near fields.
Hilling: Build high soil hills around stems to prevent spores from reaching tubers.
Weather Alert Monitoring: Spray protectants prior to forecasted wet/humid weather spells.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato Plant
symptoms: Vibrant green, sturdy leaves free of dark spots, yellowing, or leaf curl
Normal foliage structure and healthy stem growth
Potato___healthy.favorable_conditions: Optimal sunlight (6-8 hours daily), balanced NPK soil nutrition, well-drained soil (pH 5.5 - 6.5), and consistent moisture.
organic_treatments: Maintain Soil Health: Apply well-rotted organic compost or vermicompost.
Foliar Feed: Apply liquid kelp/seaweed extract every 2-3 weeks for stem vigor.
chemical_treatments: Balanced Fertilization: Apply NPK (10-10-10 or 5-10-10) according to soil test recommendations.
prevention_tips: Regular Scouting: Inspect plants twice weekly for early signs of pests or disease.
Mulching: Apply straw mulch to retain moisture, suppress weeds, and prevent soil splashing.
Proper Watering: Water deeply at soil level in early mornings.
